references.text: Describes the actual resurrection of Lazarus, which is the reason the crowd comes to see him in John 12:9.
States that many of the Jews who had seen what Jesus did believed in him, explaining the motivation for the crowd in John 12:9.
Recalls that the witnesses to Lazarus' resurrection were the reason the crowd met Jesus, a direct parallel to the motive in John 12:9.
Shows how the resurrection of Lazarus led the chief priests and Pharisees to gather to discuss the consequences, creating the context for the great attention in John 12:9.
Describes that the chief priests planned to kill Lazarus as well because many Jews were turning away on account of him, emphasizing Lazarus' central role as a draw in John 12:9.
